evidence: src/infrastructure/app.ts: createApp() creates InMemoryUserRepository, InMemoryProjectRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository, then passes them into CreateProjectUseCase, CreateTaskUseCase, AssignTaskUseCase, MarkTaskAsDoneUseCase and ListTasksUseCase.

src/infrastructure/app.ts: each route (app.post('/projects'), app.post('/tasks'), app.post('/tasks/assign'), app.post('/tasks/done'), app.get('/projects/:projectId/tasks')) calls a ProjectController or TaskController method, so no layer is skipped.
src/infrastructure/app.ts: seedUsers(userRepository: InMemoryUserRepository) only builds User entities and saves them through userRepository.save. It is bootstrap data, not a copied business rule.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit is one file, src/infrastructure/app.ts, and it handles one concern: it is the composition root. createApp builds the in-memory repositories, injects them into the use cases, injects the use cases into the controllers and binds the controllers to Express routes. It holds no business rules or invariants, so nothing is copied from the domain or application layers. Routes go through the controller methods rather than calling use cases or repositories directly, so the module's own abstractions are used as intended. The seedUsers helper adds bootstrap data, which is part of startup wiring and not a separate concern. It is typed against the concrete InMemoryUserRepository instead of a repository port. That is a small coupling choice, but a composition root may reasonably depend on concrete classes, so it is not a violation.
